ideas.name: Eni S.p.A.
ideas.thesis: Gas-weighted major with record-low gearing (9%), rising production and a satellite model (Plenitude, Enilive) that funds transition growth without touching the dividend. Ordinary dividend €1.10 (~4.7%), plus €0.46 special and €3.8 bn buyback in 2026.
ideas.bull: Production growth 7%, gearing 9% makes the €1.10 dividend safe even at $60 Brent; satellites raised €5.9 bn in 2025 and target >€5 bn EBITDA combined by 2030; buybacks ~5% of market cap/year.
ideas.bear: Peak-cycle earnings from a Middle East price spike; stock already +64% in a year and at the top of its range; special dividend and buyback shrink when Brent normalises; refining/chemicals in structural decline; Italian windfall-tax and golden-power risk; 26% Italian withholding tax with 11% only reclaimable by hand.
ideas.kill: Ordinary dividend cut below €1.10; gearing back above 20%; Enilive/Plenitude EBITDA guidance for 2026 (€1.1 bn / €1.3 bn) missed by >20%; Italy introduces a new windfall tax on energy profits; Brent below $65 for two consecutive quarters without a cut to capex.

notes.text: Logged at 52-week high after Q3 2026 (adj. net profit €2.8 bn, +125% YoY). Next review after FY2026 results and the 2027 dividend/buyback guidance.

ideas.thesis: Core dividend-quality holding: asset-light concentrate model, 33% operating margin, 60+ years of dividend increases, and currently real volume growth (+5%) from emerging markets and Zero Sugar. Hold and collect; add only when the yield returns toward 3%.
ideas.bull: Q3 2026: revenue +7%, EPS +11%, volume +5%, margin +140 bps; FY guidance raised to EPS ≥11% and FCF ≥$13 bn; net leverage 1.3x; 22 straight quarters of value share gains; US withholding tax fully creditable in Germany.
ideas.bear: 26x earnings for ~10% EPS growth, yield 2.4% at the low end of its own range; 2027 refranchising headwind will flatter nothing; sugar taxes and tariff/aluminium costs; IRS transfer-pricing case with a potential $6 bn+ liability still on appeal.
ideas.kill: Global unit case volume negative for two consecutive quarters; dividend growth below 3% a year or payout ratio above 85%; operating margin falls back below 30%; adverse final IRS ruling funded by debt that pushes net leverage above 2.5x.

ideas.name: National Grid plc
ideas.sector: Utilities – regulated electricity networks (UK & US Northeast)
ideas.thesis: Regulated grid owner whose profits grow with the networks it builds: RIIO-T3 is locked in to 2031, assets grow ~10% a year and EPS 8–10% a year. The dividend grows with UK CPIH and is untouched by withholding tax for a German investor. A buy only when the yield reaches ~4.6%, because at ~3.9% it pays less than gilts.
ideas.bull: H1 FY27: capex £6.7bn (+33%), underlying EPS +22% to 36.5p, FY27 EPS guidance raised to +15–16% (~90p). RIIO-T3 accepted (base RoE 5.70% real, management targets >9% incl. incentives). £70bn+ five-year plan. Joulent (35%, US data-centre power, Microsoft 20-yr PPA) adds growth. UK withholding tax 0%, beta ~0.6.
ideas.bear: ~3.9% yield sits below the 10y gilt (~5.1%) while the BoE is hiking again. Net debt £48.6bn and rising ~£4bn per half, gearing heading to 65%. The 2024 £7bn rights issue at 645p rebased the dividend, and another raise is possible. DPS grows only with CPIH and is diluted by scrip. UK bill-affordability politics and US rate cases. Mega-project overrun risk. Near 30-year highs. 0.5% UK stamp duty on purchase.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if: the dividend grows below UK CPIH in any year or is rebased; any new equity raise beyond scrip; regulatory gearing above 70% or any credit-rating downgrade; the 8–10% EPS CAGR framework (to FY31) is cut; UK Electricity Transmission RoE reported below 8% in two consecutive years.

ideas.name: Realty Income Corporation
ideas.sector: Real estate – net-lease REIT (retail/industrial, US + Europe)
ideas.thesis: The Monthly Dividend Company: 15,500+ net-lease properties, 98.8% occupied, with tenants paying taxes, insurance and maintenance. Pays ~5.5% yield (annualized $3.258) at ~73% of 2026 AFFO guidance of $4.45–4.46. Growth comes from buying properties at 6.8% cash yields with a ~170 bp spread over its cost of capital. For a German investor the cleanest foreign dividend: 15% US withholding, fully credited, no manual reclaim.
ideas.bull: Occupancy 98.8%, rent recapture 103.5% on re-leases, 2026 AFFO guidance raised, $10bn investment target intact, equity needs for 2026 prefunded, Europe now ~40% of deal flow with less competition. 55-year record, 644+ consecutive monthly dividends. A rate-cut cycle re-rates bond proxies like this one upward.
ideas.bear: External-growth model: total AFFO grows ~10% but per-share only 3–4% because of constant share issuance; same-store rent growth of 1.1% is below inflation. Pivot into loans, preferred equity and a private fund adds credit risk (provisions up to $14.2m from $11.6m). Retail tenant concentration (dollar stores, pharmacies, convenience). Analysts cooling: Scotiabank downgrade to Sector Perform ($59 PT), Stifel PT cut to $63.75. Highly rate-sensitive; 52-week range $53–68.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if: AFFO per share growth falls below 2% for a full year; occupancy drops below 97.5%; net debt/EBITDAre rises above 6.0x; credit-loss provisions on loans/preferred equity exceed $25m in a single quarter; or the monthly dividend is frozen for more than 12 months.

notes.text: Logged at $59.50 (close 2026-11-05), three days after Q3 2026 results (AFFO $1.12, guidance raised by $0.01). Yield 5.5%, P/AFFO ~13.4x. Buy-below $54 = ~6% yield / ~12x AFFO, roughly the 52-week low. Next review after FY2026 results and 2027 guidance (late Feb 2027).

ideas.name: Münchener Rück (Munich Re)
ideas.thesis: World's largest reinsurer with a 298% solvency ratio, 18% ROE and a stated policy of paying out >80% of profit via dividend plus buyback. Dividend €24 (~4.05% at €592), only ~47% of earnings, grown from €9.80 to €24 in six years and never cut since the 1960s. German stock: zero withholding-tax friction for me. Ambition 2030 targets >8% EPS growth from less cyclical segments (Life & Health Re, ERGO, Specialty).
ideas.bull: Record 2025 (€6.1bn), 2026 guidance raised to €6.6bn after Q3 beat; €2.25bn buyback shrinks share count ~3%/yr; P/E ~11 for an 18% ROE business; diversification away from P&C cat reinsurance lowers earnings volatility; capital return is structural with solvency ~300%.
ideas.bear: Bought at a 12-month high after +15% since October; P&C reinsurance pricing is softening (Jan renewals volume −8%) and 2026 earnings benefit from below-average cat losses; analyst average target €554 is below the price (RBC 530, UBS 515); one mega-cat or casualty reserve charge can cost 10–15% quickly; dividend growth will slow to EPS growth (high single digits), the 20% hikes are over.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if: the dividend is cut or frozen; Solvency II falls below 200%; P&C reinsurance combined ratio exceeds 95% for two consecutive years; group ROE drops below 14% for a full year; or 2027 net profit guidance comes in below €6.3bn without a major cat event explaining it.

notes.text: Logged at ~€592 (close 2026-11-05, Tradegate; Xetra within a euro) after the Q3 pre-release raised 2026 guidance to €6.6bn. Final Q3 on 12 Nov 2026. Buy-below €535 = 4.5% yield / ~10.5x 2026 EPS. Next review after FY2026 results and the 2026 dividend proposal (late Feb 2027).

ideas.name: Brookfield Renewable Partners (→ BEP Inc. after simplification)
ideas.sector: Utilities – renewable power / yieldco (hydro, wind, solar, storage, nuclear)
ideas.thesis: Global renewable platform with contracted, inflation-linked cash flows: 10% FFO/unit CAGR and 6% distribution CAGR since 2012, LTM FFO $2.18/unit, distribution $1.57 (5.1% yield, ~72% payout). 85.7 GW advanced pipeline (~$1.0bn FFO net), hyperscaler demand, $5.1bn liquidity. Simplification into one Canadian corp (BEP Inc., vote 30 Nov 2026) should widen the buyer base; BEP units trade ~2% below BEPC for the same future share.
ideas.bull: 5.1% yield + 5–9% distribution growth gives ~10%/yr without re-rating; 14x FFO is below own history after a rate-driven sell-off from $38; Boralex, Aypa storage and Westinghouse nuclear add growth; Microsoft 10.5 GW framework; index inclusion after simplification.
ideas.bear: FFO includes asset-sale gains (Maine hydro, Isagen) so true payout is tighter than 72%; unit count +3.4%/yr dilution treadmill; bond-proxy rate sensitivity; sponsor fees/incentive distributions to BAM; El Niño hydrology in Colombia; US tax-credit rollbacks; Q3 revenue miss; IFRS net losses. Tax: ~7.5% effective WHT as LP, after simplification 25% Canadian WHT (15% creditable, 10% reclaim by hand); unit→share exchange may be booked as a taxable sale by Trade Republic.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if: distribution growth drops below 5% or is cut; FFO payout ratio excluding asset-sale gains exceeds 85%; the simplification fails on 30 Nov and the dual structure persists; credit rating falls below BBB; unit count grows >5%/yr while FFO/unit growth falls below 7%.

notes.text: 2026-11-06: Logged at $30.64 (NYSE close 5 Nov). BEPC $31.27. Watch: BEP unitholder vote 30 Nov 2026 (proxy deadline 25 Nov), closing expected Q4 2026. Decide then: buy BEP Inc. as clean Canadian corp vs. BEP units now for the ~2% discount.

ideas.name: Daikin Industries
ideas.thesis: Global #1 HVAC, 84% sales abroad. Dividend-growth compounder, not income: DPS ¥200 (FY3/22) → ¥370 (FY3/27e), ~13% CAGR, payout ~39%, 16y no cut. Activist catalyst: Elliott ~3% stake (Apr 2026) → ¥350bn buyback (~5.5% of mkt cap), ROE target 12%, higher payout pledged. Buy below ¥19,500 = ~20x FY3/27e EPS ¥957, 1.9% yield on ¥370 / 2.0% on ~¥390 consensus next year.
ideas.bull: H1 FY3/27: sales +17.4% to ¥2.91tn, OP +9.8% record; FY OP guide raised to ¥455bn, DPS ¥360→¥370. P/E ~22x vs 5y median ~25x; price in lower half of 52w range (17,380–26,440), ATH 31,330 (2023). Structural demand: heat pumps, heat, data-center chillers, India. Absorbed ~¥41bn US tariff hit via pricing/costs. Held +1.5% on the -6% Nikkei day (6 Nov).
ideas.bear: Yield only 1.7%, ~23x fwd P/E for an 8.4% OP margin, so a re-rating needs margin expansion that's still unproven. Guide assumes ¥155/$, so weak yen flatters earnings. US residential weak (rates); data-center moratoria fears hit the growth leg. Chemicals OP -28% last FY; PFAS regulation/liability tail. Equity ratio 55.9%→51.0%. Tax: JP 15.315% WHT, DE credits 15%, so ~0.3% lost; the full 15% is lost on dividends inside the Sparerpauschbetrag.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if OP margin stays ≤8.5% through FY3/28 despite pricing, the buyback/payout pledges stall after Elliott's pressure fades, DPS growth drops below ~5%/yr, or PFAS liabilities turn material.

ideas.name: Zoetis
ideas.thesis: World #1 animal-health company (~$9.3B sales 2026e), priced like a melting ice cube: ~13x EPS, ~6.9% FCF yield after -34% YTD. The cash engine is intact: FCF/share 3.51 -> 5.05 -> 5.14 (2023-25), payout ~35% of earnings, buybacks ~4%/yr, net debt ~1.9x EBITDA. Buy below $82 = 25% off a ~$110 base: 17x 2026e adj. EPS $6.30 = $107; FCF $5.61/sh growing 3% at an 8% hurdle = $116. At $82 the market implies ~1% FCF growth forever. Yield 2.6% vs ~1% historically.
ideas.bull: Livestock (+8% in Q3) and diagnostics are growing; Q3 2026 beat ($1.75 adj. EPS vs $1.51 expected), FY adj. EPS guide raised to $6.25-6.35, some 2027 approvals pulled into Q4 2026. If U.S. companion animal merely stabilises: 18-20x on ~$6.5 = $115-130 plus a growing 2.6% yield.
ideas.bear: U.S. segment -6% in Q3 (pet owners cutting vet visits, competitive pressure in dermatology, i.e. its Apoquel/Cytopoint franchise). 2026 organic revenue -1 to -2%, adj. net income -5 to -7%, management cautious on 2027 (stock -8% on results day). Bear value: $5.25 EPS x 12 = ~$63 (52w low $68.77). Tax: US 15% withheld, fully credited in DE via W-8BEN, no loss.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if 2027 guidance has adj. EPS below $5.75, or U.S. companion animal is still shrinking in H2 2027 - then it's erosion, not a pause.

The numbers keep compounding: 9M 2026 organic +6%, adj. operating profit +10% cc, FCF/share 4.96 -> 5.62 -> 5.88 (2023-25), net debt 2.0x EBITDA, dividend EUR 2.52 (+8%). Buy below EUR 88 = 25% off a ~EUR 117 base: 20x 2026e adj. EPS ~EUR 5.60 = EUR 112; adj. FCF EUR 1.30-1.35B = ~EUR 5.95/sh growing 3% at an 8% hurdle = EUR 123. At EUR 90 the market implies ~1.3% growth forever. Yield 2.8% vs ~1.9% in 2025.

ideas.name: VICI Properties
ideas.thesis: Triple-net landlord of Caesars Palace, MGM Grand, the Venetian and ~90 more; 100% occupancy, ~40-yr leases, ~2% escalators, about half CPI-linked. 2026 AFFO $2.47-2.48/sh, dividend $1.84 (7.3%), payout ~75%, 9 straight raises, net debt 4.8x EBITDA, first $2B buyback. Buy below $22.50 = 25% off a ~$30 base: 12x 2027e AFFO ~$2.56 = $31; dividend growing 2.5% at an 8% hurdle = $34; haircut for Caesars. NOT in the buy zone today (was $22.73 two weeks ago); by my estimate the score crosses 75 around $24.70.
ideas.bull: Rent is contractual and covered; AFFO/sh still +4%; buying back stock at ~10x AFFO is accretive; any clean Caesars outcome re-rates to 13-14x = $33-36.
ideas.bear: Caesars (~38% of rent; regional + Joliet lease ~$740M/yr) is being bought by Fertitta, got downgraded, VICI booked a $313M credit-loss allowance and openly weighs fixing or selling that lease. A 25% cut on it = -$0.17 AFFO/sh -> 9x on $2.30 = ~$21. Refinancing gets dearer (new notes at 5.42%). Tax: US 15% withheld, credited in DE; the whole payout is taxed as dividend income.
ideas.kill: I'm wrong if the Caesars regional rent is cut by more than 30%, or 2027 AFFO per share falls.
